clip_script: Call me the Algebra Grandmaster. I teach Maths at Supacharge. Here's what I do to arithmetic sequences. You want the distinction? You start with the formula: T_n = a + (n - 1)d. That is your primary tool. Every arithmetic sequence problem is fundamentally a system defined by three variables: the first term 'a', the constant difference 'd', and the position 'n' with its value 'T_n'. If they give you any three, you can always solve for the fourth. Master this relationship, state your formula first to secure your method mark, and you control the topic.
